prompt: A stateless web app runs on one server that's at 100% CPU at peak. You can add more identical servers.
why: Put a load balancer in front of a pool of identical servers.
trap: Sharding splits data, but this app holds no state to split.

prompt: Some app servers occasionally hang, and users who land on them see errors until someone restarts them.
why: Health checks take bad servers out of rotation automatically.
trap: A circuit breaker is the caller protecting itself from a dependency, not routing users away from bad hosts.

prompt: You want to deploy new versions during the day without dropping requests.
why: Drain servers one at a time behind the balancer while the rest keep serving.
trap: A queue can buffer background work, but live HTTP requests need somewhere to go now.

prompt: Twenty app servers each manage their own TLS certificates and keep drifting out of date. Traffic is growing.
why: Terminate TLS once at the load balancer and spread traffic to the servers behind it.
trap: A CDN can terminate TLS for cached content, but dynamic app traffic still needs balancing.

prompt: Some requests take 10 ms and others 10 seconds. Round-robin leaves some servers swamped with long ones while others sit idle.
trap: The fix is in how the balancer picks, not adding limits.

prompt: Run the new version on a separate set of servers and switch all traffic over at once, with instant rollback by switching back.
tells: switch all traffic over at once
why: Blue-green deploys are a load balancer target switch.
trap: It's a deploy strategy built on the balancer.

prompt: Requests to /api should go to one server pool and /images to another, based on the URL path.
tells: /api should go to one server pool
why: A layer 7 (HTTP) load balancer routes by path.
trap: Sharding splits data; this splits requests by route.

prompt: Users should be sent to the nearest healthy region, and away from a region that goes down.
tells: away from a region that goes down
why: Global load balancing (DNS or anycast) with health checks.
trap: The CDN caches content; this routes live traffic across regions.
